issue.title: Locate the D 61 M 48 kf 23 extra zeros in B1b and B1c

labels.name: mac
labels.description: Task for mac, the coordinator's M5 Mac

issue.body:
**What.** Locate the extra zeros of det M at D 61.03, M 48, kf 23 in B1b (3 conjugate pairs) and B1c (1 pair), from #212's cached samples, and confirm each with a small circle. A circle around λ_phys is the control (+1). Recommended by macm3 in #212's summary.

**Why.** #212 found 24 zeros beyond the expected ones, 8 of them with 1.27 < Re λ < 6.6 and |Im λ| < ω/2. Their positions say whether they look like modes (isolated, and stable as the cut changes) or like a ring of the weak directions (a regular row that follows the cut).

**Code first (Mac subagent).** `hp/modecount_moment.py` gives only the first moment (one zero), for B1c and U, and reads only `hp/data`. It gets the higher moments (power sums, then Newton's identities), the box B1b and `--data`, with a planted test that can fail. `hp/modecount_circle.py` gets `--data`. The same moments on #159's kf 21 cache cost no new determinants and show whether the zeros move with the cut.

**Acceptance (can fail).** Each zero's position, with its circle's winding (+1 each). The λ_phys circle winds +1. The sum of the windings matches #212's B1b +6 and B1c +2.

**Depends on.** #212.

comments.body: started (2026-11-09 06:37 UTC). Machine: mac (Apple M5, 10 cores, shared with #208's two CAPD processes). Checkout: worktree `.claude/worktrees/agent-a532f23762bc68577` (branch `worktree-agent-a532f23762bc68577`, from main f88c372), backed up to `wip/i230`. Threads: at most 2 processes of 1 thread each, `nice -n 10`. Python: venv-314 (3.14). Plan: moment code and its planted test first, then the moments on #212's kf 23 and #159's kf 21 caches (no new determinants), then the circles (new determinants), raw output in `I230-mac/`.

Progress (07:05 UTC, mac). Utilization: my 2 circle processes at 98% cpu each (0.2% memory each); the machine is at 73% cpu, 30 of 32 GB used (others' processes).

**Code** (branch `wip/i230`). `hp/modecount_moment.py` now gives every zero inside B1b or B1c (power sums to the winding, Newton's identities, roots), with `--data`. It locates on two contours, the upper half (with the count's real-axis samples, 0.5 apart) and the whole box mirrored (no real-axis sample), with a local cubic rule. `hp/modecount_circle.py` takes `--data` and gives the positions of the zeros inside a circle that winds 1–3 times (periodic trapezoid sums of ln(det M/(λ−c)^W)).

**Planted tests.** Both have their controls, which fail as they must.

- Moment test, first version: FAIL. Its error estimate (cubic against trapezoid) was 10–100 times too pessimistic.
- Second version: FAIL. The new estimate (the spread over cubic stencils and the two contours) was below the true error in 5 of 8 random cases, by up to 4 times. With three zeros close together in B1b the error reached 0.45.
- Third version: PASS on 23 cases, 12 of them held out (drawn with a new seed, first run under these criteria). Every root with spread < 0.05 is within 0.05 of its planted zero, and 57 of 76 planted zeros get such a root. So the spread flags a root good enough to centre a circle; it is an estimator range, not an error bar.
- Circle test: positions within 1e-5 or better, with estimates that cover the error. Its second version failed one case at n0 = 16 (estimate 1.3e-3 > 1e-3). The circles run at n0 = 20, which passes every case.

**Discrepancy found by the planted test (count code, not this task's boxes).** `modecount_wind.py` can miss whole 2π turns on the long edge Im = 3ω/2 (T). There the phase of g grows by 11–20 rad per unit of Re, so an interval of the initial grid (0.57) turns by about 2π, looks flat, and is never bisected or verified. It did so in 6 of 20 random planted cases, giving wrong U and full windings while every edge reported "resolved". In #212's kf 23 record, the last two intervals of T (Re 1.157→0.300, spacings 0.29 and 0.57, steps +0.04 and +0.23 rad) were never bisected, while the phase grows by about 17 rad/unit just before them and 20 rad/unit on T0 just after. So #212's kf 23 **U +8 and full +24 are suspect**. B1b and B1c do not use T, and their edges were all bisected at least twice. #159's kf 21 T is refined everywhere (spacing ≤ 0.036). I will re-sample that stretch (about 30 determinants) after the circles.

**Moments, from the caches (no new determinants).** Positions are of the zero in the upper half. The conjugates follow by symmetry. The spread is an estimator range.

| zero | kf 21 (#159) | spread | kf 23 (#212) | spread | moved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.3490 + 1.4308i (B1b) | 1.6e-2 | 1.3064 + 1.4164i (B1b) | 2.3e-3 | 0.045 |
| 2 | 2.0926 + 1.0168i (B1b) | 2.0e-2 | 2.0073 + 0.9735i (B1b) | 2.5e-3 | 0.096 |
| 3 | 2.6914 + 0.4565i (B1c, 0.05 right of Re = a2) | 8.9e-3 | 2.5589 + 0.5822i (B1b) | 1.8e-3 | 0.183 |
| 4 | none | | 3.019 + (0.03 to 0.09)i (B1c) | 6.8e-2 | new |

Windings of the moment contours: B1b 2 (kf 21) and 3 (kf 23) upper zeros, B1c 1 and 1, matching #212's +4/+6 and +2/+2. Zero 4 sits within 0.1 of the real axis: ln|g| at λ = 3.0 is −4.3 at kf 23 against −1.1 at kf 21.

**Running now.** Two processes compute circles at kf 23 (n0 = 20, R = 0.2): λ_phys (control), zeros 1, 2, 3, and a circle on the real axis at 3.019 that should wind +2 for the pair 4. They take about 67 s per determinant. Then come the T stretch, and circles at kf 21 (its three zeros and λ_phys), so that the shifts are measured precisely and against λ_phys's own shift. #212's determinants are reproduced here to 1.3e-8 in ln|det M| (criterion 1e-8, failed narrowly). This machine's own two LUs (crate against hpkernel) differ by 1.5e-5 on the same matrix, so the cross-machine difference is within rounding noise. Phase differences are below 1e-9 rad.

Progress (08:09 UTC, mac). Utilization: 2 circle processes at 100% cpu, 0.3% memory each; machine 52% cpu, 30 of 32 GB used. 92 new determinants so far, about 110 s each under the load.

**Circles at kf 23 (M 48, n0 20, R 0.2).**

| circle | winding of det M | points | max step | zeros inside (estimate) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| λ_phys = 2.043532530673195 (control) | **+1** | 28 + 2 | 0.376 rad | 2.0435328121 − 1.4e-7 i (5.5e-7) |
| 3.01943 on the real axis | **+2** | 42 + 2 | 0.401 rad | 3.019571 ± 0.095819 i (7e-6) |

The control passes: one zero, at λ_phys to 2.8e-7, within the estimate. Zero 4 is a conjugate pair at 3.0196 ± 0.0958i, 0.096 from the real axis. The mirrored-box moment had put it at 3.0194 + 0.0939i (0.002 off). The half contour, which uses the 0.5-spaced real-axis samples, put it at Im 0.026; its spread of 0.068 had flagged it. Zeros 1, 2 and 3 are running.

**Coordinator's request (#238).** `hp/modecount_moment.py` now locates in every box of the count: B0, B1a, B1b, B1c, B1, full, U0 and U (704aa75). It gives B1b and B1c output identical to before. The planted test gained left-column cases (B0, U0, U), seven of them first run under a new criterion (e). **U0 passed (e). B0 failed it** in one of 7 cases: a root with spread 9.4e-6 lay 0.052 from its planted zero. In the other left cases B0's errors (up to 2.7e-2) exceeded its spreads by up to 40 times. B0 has no half contour (the count has no real-axis samples left of aL), so its spread comes from the cubic stencils alone, and those miss the error of the sample spacing. B0 is now printed, not tested (98096fb). Its moment roots are good to about 0.05 and need circles, which `modecount_circle.py` gives precisely. Logs are in `I230-mac/planted/`.

Progress (09:15 UTC, mac). Utilization: 2 processes at 100% cpu each, 0.3% memory each; machine 69% cpu, 30 of 32 GB used. The kf 23 circles are all done: 5 circles, 155 determinants, every one wound as expected, 0 verification mismatches.

| circle (centre, R 0.2) | winding of det M | points | max step | zero(s) inside | estimate | distance from the moment position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| λ_phys 2.043532530673195 (control) | **+1** | 28 + 2 | 0.376 | 2.0435328121 − 1.4e-7 i | 5.5e-7 | 3.1e-7 |
| zero 1: 1.30641 + 1.41644i | **+1** | 27 + 2 | 0.389 | 1.306478 + 1.415783i | 9.3e-7 | 6.6e-4 |
| zero 2: 2.00728 + 0.97347i | **+1** | 29 + 2 | 0.363 | 2.007279 + 0.972720i | 4.9e-7 | 7.5e-4 |
| zero 3: 2.55894 + 0.58224i | **+1** | 29 + 2 | 0.368 | 2.558385 + 0.582474i | 5.0e-7 | 6.0e-4 |
| zero 4: 3.01943 on the real axis | **+2** | 42 + 2 | 0.401 | 3.019571 ± 0.095819i | 7e-6 | 1.9e-3 |

The estimates come from the n0/2-point sums. They are conservative in the planted test, where they covered the error in every case. With the conjugates, B1b holds 3 pairs (+6) and B1c 1 pair (+2), as #212 counted.

Running now: the T stretch (#212's possible missed turns; 10 of about 35 determinants done), and circles at kf 21 around λ_phys and zero 3's kf 21 position, then zeros 1 and 2. They measure the shift between the cuts against λ_phys's own shift.

Progress (10:27 UTC, mac). Utilization: 2 processes (T stretch, kf 21 circles) at 100% cpu when awake, 0.3% memory each; machine 76% cpu, 31 of 32 GB used.

**Stall.** The Mac went into maintenance sleep at 09:55 UTC, with dark wakes every 15 min. One determinant took 986 s. My runs had no sleep assertion. They now run under `caffeinate -i -w <pid>`, as #212's runs did. Nothing was lost (the caches are written per determinant). They are only late.

**kf 21 control.** The circle |λ − λ_phys| = 0.2 at kf 21 winds **+1** (28 + 2 points, max step 0.382 rad, 0 mismatches). The zero is at 2.0435324951 + 1.9e-8 i (estimate 1.2e-7). At kf 23 it was 2.0435328121 − 1.4e-7 i (estimate 5.5e-7). **λ_phys moves by 3.2e-7 between the cuts, within the estimates. The extra zeros move by 0.045 to 0.18.**

Running: the T stretch (52 determinants so far; it is bisecting near Re 0.6–0.85, where the phase turns fast), and the kf 21 circle around zero 3 (2.69136 + 0.45650i). Zeros 1 and 2 at kf 21 follow.

**Discrepancy (10:40 UTC, mac): #212's kf 23 count missed 3 turns on the edge Im = 3ω/2. U is +11, not +8, and full is +30, not +24.**

`I230-mac/t_check.py` re-sampled the stretch of T that the kf 23 count had left at the initial spacing, Re 1.157 → 0.300 at Im 5.2151. It used the count's rules: spacing 0.03, bisection to steps ≤ π/4, then verification of every step > π/8. That took 62 new determinants, 65 points, max step 0.381 rad and 0 mismatches. The phase change of g there is **+19.119 rad**, where the count's two steps gave +0.270: **+3.0000 turns** hidden. With it, T goes from +97.21 to +116.06 rad, **U wind(g) from +8 to +11**, and **full from +24 to +30**. The reading rule was fixed in the script before the run. B1b and B1c do not use T and stand.

So the extras at D 61, M 48 are **24 at kf 21 and 30 at kf 23**, not 24 at both:

| cut | B1b | B1c | B1 | U (each strip) | full |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| kf 21 (#159, #212) | +4 | +2 | +6 | +9 | +24 |
| kf 23 (#212 as recorded) | +6 | +2 | +8 | +8 | +24 |
| kf 23 (T re-sampled here) | +6 | +2 | +8 | **+11** | **+30** |

Two points from #212's reading change.

- "Windings add: full 24 = B1 8 + U 8 + mirror 8" cannot fail. full, B1 and U share their edges, and full = B1 + 2U is an identity of the edge sums. So it was no check, and it held with the missed turns too.
- "One zero per strip entering B1b across Im = ±1.738" is not what happened. The B1b gain is zero 3 crossing Re = a2 from B1c (2.691 + 0.457i at kf 21 → 2.558 + 0.582i at kf 23). B1c's new pair at 3.0196 ± 0.0958i came from elsewhere. U gained 2 per strip, so the extra zeros multiply as the cut rises.

`I230-mac/alias_scan.py` compares each interval's step with its neighbours' rates. On every edge of both records it flags only these two intervals at kf 23 (its control). At kf 21 it flags one interval of V2 (Re a2, Im 0 → 0.29), next to zero 3, which sits 0.048 from V2 at Im 0.457. ln|g| there is smooth (−2.03 → −2.48), so this reads as the steep phase near that zero, not a hidden turn. The kf 21 circle around zero 3 (running) covers that region. The count code's weakness (an interval that looks flat is never checked) is for the coordinator: see the recommended task in the closing summary.

## Closing summary (11:21 UTC, mac)

Every extra zero in B1b and B1c at D 61.03, M 48, kf 23 is located and confirmed by a small circle, and so is each at kf 21. They form a regular row that moves with the cut, by 1.7×10⁵ to 5×10⁵ times λ_phys's own shift. A new member appears at kf 23. The λ_phys controls wind +1 at both cuts. Separately, #212's kf 23 count missed 3 turns on the edge Im = 3ω/2, so the extras there total 30, not 24. All my processes have ended; the machine is now at 34% cpu, 30 of 32 GB used.

### Zeros (circles: n0 20, R 0.2, 0 verification mismatches each)

Positions are in the upper half; the conjugates follow from det M(λ̄) = conj det M(λ). The estimate is the distance to the n0/2-point value, which was conservative in the planted test.

| zero | kf 21 position (circle winding) | kf 23 position (circle winding) | shift |
|---|---|---|---|
| λ_phys (control) | 2.0435324951 + 1.9e-8 i (**+1**, est. 1.2e-7) | 2.0435328121 − 1.4e-7 i (**+1**, est. 5.5e-7) | 3.2e-7 |
| 1 (B1b) | 1.3559634 + 1.4385362i (**+1**, 1.0e-6) | 1.3064778 + 1.4157830i (**+1**, 9.3e-7) | 0.0545 |
| 2 (B1b) | 2.0868804 + 0.9897338i (**+1**, 2.3e-7) | 2.0072792 + 0.9727203i (**+1**, 4.9e-7) | 0.0814 |
| 3 | 2.6897138 + 0.4760982i, B1c, 0.046 right of Re = a2 (**+1**, 6.2e-8) | 2.5583853 + 0.5824738i, B1b (**+1**, 5.0e-7) | 0.1690 |
| 4 (B1c) | none | 3.0195705 ± 0.0958190i, one circle on the real axis (**+2**, 7e-6) | new |

The sums match #212. At kf 23, B1b holds 3 pairs (+6) and B1c 1 pair (+2). At kf 21, B1b holds 2 pairs (+4) and B1c 1 pair (+2). Both controls pass: λ_phys winds +1 at both cuts and moves by 3.2e-7, within the estimates. It sits 3.6e-8 (kf 21) and 2.8e-7 (kf 23) from the M 32 value 2.043532530673195.

### Reading

**The data support a regular row that follows the truncation, not isolated modes.**

- At kf 23 the four zeros lie along one curve, from 1.31 + 1.42i down to 3.02 + 0.10i. Neighbours are 0.83, 0.68 and 0.67 apart.
- From kf 21 to kf 23 every member moves to smaller Re, by 0.054, 0.081 and 0.169. The shift grows along the row, and zero 3 crosses from B1c into B1b. A new member appears at the lower end, 0.096 from the real axis.
- With the T correction, the total of extras goes from 24 to 30 (B1 +6 → +8, each strip U +9 → +11).
- None of the extras stays put. λ_phys moves 1.7×10⁵ times less than the least-moved extra.

**What it does not show.**

- A mode whose eigenfunction has weight in centre harmonics 22–23 would also move when they are unpinned. The cut test cannot separate that from an artifact, the same limit as at D 30 (MODE_COUNT section 5). The third resolution (#231) can.
- The zeros in U (11 per strip at kf 23) are not located: the moment code is not reliable with 8 or more zeros in a strip.
- Whether the pair at 3.02 ± 0.096i reaches the real axis at another cut and becomes two real zeros.
- Anything at other D or M.

Status: numerical evidence at one D and one M. It makes a truncation origin of the D 61 extras likely, and it does not restore the one-unstable-mode statement at M 48.

### Planted tests

`hp/modecount_moment_planted.py`, the moment code. Logs are in `I230-mac/planted/`.

- **v1 FAIL.** The error estimate (cubic against trapezoid) was 10–100 times too pessimistic.
- **v2 FAIL.** The spread was below the error in 5 of 8 random cases, by up to 4 times.
- **v3 PASS**, on 12 held-out cases plus the development cases. Every root with spread < 0.05 lies within 0.05, and 57 of 76 planted zeros got one.
- **v4 FAIL in B0**, one of 7 new left-column cases: error 0.052 with spread 9.4e-6. B0 has no half contour, so its spread comes from the stencils alone.
- **v5 PASS**, with B0 printed, not tested.
- Mutations `--mutate=nok` (drops the factor k of the integration by parts) and `--mutate=shift` (zeros planted 0.1 off) **fail, as they must**.

`hp/modecount_circle_planted.py`, the circles.

- **v1 PASS.**
- **v2 FAIL** at n0 16 in the two-zero case: estimate 1.3e-3 > 1e-3, error 6.3e-5.
- **v3 PASS** at n0 20, the real circles' setting. Positions are within 1.4e-5 or better, with estimates that cover the error.
- Mutations `--mutate=nodiv` and `--mutate=offset` (0.01) **fail, as they must**.

On the real data the moment positions sit 6e-4 to 1.9e-3 (kf 23) and 1.0e-2 to 2.8e-2 (kf 21) from the circles. At kf 21 the spread was below the error for 2 of 3 zeros, by up to 2.2 times. So the spread is a flag, not an error bar. The circles give the positions.

### What ran (all exits 0 unless noted)

- Moments on #212's kf 23 cache and #159's kf 21 cache (re-evaluated in #212), with no new determinants.
- 9 circles, 285 determinants, in runs A, B, C, D and E. D was stopped by me after its first circle, and its second ran as E.
- The T stretch, 62 determinants.
- `repro_check.py` (exit 1, see below) and `noise_check.py`, 4 determinants.
- `alias_scan.py` on both records.
- 351 new determinants in all, single-threaded under nice 10, at most 2 determinant processes. Short analysis scripts (seconds each) ran beside them.

### Raw folder

`I230-mac/`: raw commits db34383 and **e7dc533** (on GitHub). Code: branch `wip/i230`, commits 38ab804 … **98096fb**.

### Discrepancies (reported, not fixed)

1. **#212 kf 23: U +11 and full +30, not +8 and +24.** T missed 3 turns in Re 1.157 → 0.300 (my 10:37 comment has the details). #212's check "full 24 = B1 8 + U 8 + mirror 8" is an identity of the shared edges and cannot fail. "One zero per strip entering B1b across Im = ±1.738" is not what happened: zero 3 crossed Re = a2. The README and MODE_COUNT section 5 quote the old kf 23 row.
2. **`modecount_wind.py` can hide whole turns.** An interval whose step looks flat is never bisected or verified. Where the phase grows by 11–20 rad per unit (the edge T at M 48, h0 0.6), an initial interval of 0.57 can turn by 2πk. This happened in 6 of 20 random planted cases, with every edge reporting "resolved".
3. `repro_check.py`, criterion 1e-8 fixed before the run: **failed narrowly**. #212's determinants are reproduced here to 1.3e-8 in ln|det M| and 8.6e-10 in arg. This machine's own two LUs (crate against hpkernel) differ by 1.5e-5 on the same matrix, so the difference is within rounding noise. It is far below what moves a winding.
4. The half contour leans on the count's real-axis samples, 0.5 apart. For zero 4 (Im 0.096) it gave Im 0.026; the mirrored contour gave 0.094.
5. Process note: the Mac went into maintenance sleep at 09:55 UTC and stalled the runs (one determinant took 986 s). Later runs used `caffeinate -i`.

### Recommended tasks

1. **`modecount_wind`: no interval left unchecked because it looks flat.**
   - What: in `edge()`, bisect every interval once, or every interval whose length times its neighbours' largest phase rate exceeds π, as `I230-mac/alias_scan.py` does. Add the planted configurations that fail now (moment test random0, random4, random7, held1, held5, held9) to `modecount_planted.py`.
   - Why: discrepancy 2. It changed #212's U and full.
   - Acceptance (can fail): those cases give the planted U and full windings, and a mutation restoring the old rule makes them fail.
   - Depends on: #230.
2. **Re-check the long edges of the other h0 0.6 counts.**
   - What: run `alias_scan.py` on the count records of #211 (D 45 kf 23), #232 (D 50, D 55: its U0 +1 and U +1 feed #238), #190, #178, #170 and I68, re-sample each flagged interval as `t_check.py` does, and restate U, U0 and full.
   - Why: those windings come from the same sampling.
   - Acceptance (can fail): the scan's control (#212 kf 23 T) is flagged, and each flagged interval is re-sampled to steps ≤ π/4 with 0 mismatches, each box stated as corrected or unchanged.
   - Depends on: #230.
3. **Follow the row through more cuts at D 61, M 48.**
   - What: circles, plus moments where a count exists, at kf 22 and kf 25 or 27, seeded from the kf 21 and kf 23 positions.
   - Why: the reading rests on two cuts. It also shows whether the pair at 3.02 ± 0.096i reaches the real axis, where it would become two real zeros.
   - Acceptance (can fail): a λ_phys circle winds +1 and sits within 1e-6 of the kf 23 value, each zero gets a +1 circle, and positions are tabulated against kf.
   - Depends on: #230, and states that converge to |F| ≤ 1e-15 at those cuts.
4. **Locate the U zeros at D 61, M 48, kf 23 (11 per strip).**
   - What: cut U by vertical edges (new determinants) into sub-boxes of at most 3 zeros, then moments and circles in each.
   - Why: to see whether all 30 extras form one ring with the B1b/B1c row.
   - Acceptance (can fail): the sub-box windings sum to the strip's +11, and each zero gets a +1 circle.
   - Depends on: task 1.

### For #238 (coordinator's note)

`hp/modecount_moment.py` now handles every box of the count (B0, B1a, B1b, B1c, B1, full, U0, U) at little cost. U0 passed its planted criterion. In B0 the moment roots are good to about 0.05 but their spread is no flag (it missed an error of 0.052), so B0 zeros need circles. `modecount_circle.py --data` gives those positions to about 1e-6.

### Proposed text for notes/MODE_COUNT.md section 5 (coordinator's call)

> **Positions (#230).** The extras in B1b and B1c at D 61, M 48 lie on one row, from 1.31 + 1.42i down to 3.02 ± 0.10i, each zero confirmed by a small circle (`hp/modecount_circle.py`, raw `I230-mac/`, e7dc533). From kf 21 to kf 23 every member moves by 0.05 to 0.17, against 3×10⁻⁷ for λ_phys. One crosses from B1c into B1b, and a new pair appears at 3.0196 ± 0.0958i. The kf 23 count's edge Im = 3ω/2 hid 3 turns, so at kf 23 U is +11 and full +30 (24 at kf 21). The extras multiply and move with the cut, which points to the truncation. A mode with weight in centre harmonics 22–23 would move too, so the third resolution (#231) decides.

The issue stays open for the coordinator; I am removing `running`.

Coordinator: reviewed and merged (wip/i230 at 7035fa0). Both planted tests pass with their controls here (`modecount_moment_planted.py --controls`, `modecount_circle_planted.py --controls`, exit 0). Recorded in notes/MODE_COUNT.md section 5 (3d0e973, d5ddb3b) and the README's open items. modecount_local.sh's job 4 now passes --allow_unraw, since the circle tool requires a raw task folder. Recommended tasks filed as #242 (check every interval), #243 (re-check the earlier counts), #244 (more cuts at D 61) and #245 (the U zeros). #238 is unblocked.
